summary: The MOE Taiwan Scholarship is a Ministry of Education (Taiwan) scheme for foreign students who want a full bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree at a university or college in Taiwan. Applicants apply to the Taiwan representative office (embassy-level office) for their country for the scholarship and separately to a Taiwanese university for admission. It pays tuition and miscellaneous fees up to a cap and a monthly living allowance, for up to 4, 2 or 4 years depending on the level.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be foreign nationals with a graduation certificate or diploma from a secondary school or post-secondary institution, an excellent academic record and good moral character. Students from Mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau are excluded from the scheme.

Not eligible: ROC nationals and overseas compatriot students; people already registered at a Taiwan university or college, or already eligible for or registered to start a degree there (a student in the final year of a degree may apply for a higher-level degree); people who already studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level they plan to enter; exchange students and dual or joint degree students admitted under inter-university agreements; people who have already held a Taiwan Scholarship for five years in total; people whose Taiwan Scholarship or MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship was ever revoked; and people who will receive any financial assistance from a Taiwan government body or an education institution in Taiwan while studying (the only exception is a university discount that covers tuition and miscellaneous fees above the MOE cap).

Grades: where the grade scale tops out at 4.5, a bachelor's applicant needs an average of at least 3.0 and a master's applicant at least 3.5. The representative office converts other grading systems to the 4.5 scale or uses a standard that universities in that country treat as excellent. No threshold is set for doctoral applicants.

Language: for programmes not fully taught in English, applicants submit a Test of Chinese as a Foreign Language (TOCFL) result or certificate at Band B level or higher (the Terms of Agreement say Level 3 or above). Other Chinese tests are not accepted. If the local office does not run TOCFL, the recipient must take the test at their own expense by the end of the first semester in Taiwan and hand the result to the university. For programmes fully taught in English, the office may waive TOCFL and ask for TOEFL scores at its set standard, or another recognised intermediate English exam (with an overall score of at least 75 percent), or a diploma from a programme fully taught in English. Citizens of countries where English is an official national language are exempt. The programme must be on the MOE English-taught checklist, or the university must give written proof that it is fully taught in English.

Offices give preference to applicants with TOCFL Band B or higher, and weigh the person's circumstances, real language ability, interpersonal manner and moral character, and whether they could contribute to Taiwan's development and to their home country. Each representative office sets its own selection regulations, number of awards and timetable.
age_experience_notes: The Directions state no age limit and no work-experience requirement.
funding_summary: The MOE pays tuition and miscellaneous fees (course-credit fees and basic study-related miscellaneous fees) up to NTD 40,000 per semester, and the student pays any excess to the university. It also pays a living allowance of NTD 15,000 per month for bachelor's students and NTD 20,000 per month for master's and doctoral students. The scholarship year runs from 1 September to 31 August. The maximum holding period is 4 years for a bachelor's, 2 years for a master's and 4 years for a doctorate, and no person may hold the scholarship for more than 5 years in total. Administration fees, thesis supervision fees, insurance, accommodation and internet access are not covered.
programmes_note: Degree programmes at Taiwanese universities and colleges, in Chinese or in English. Applicants for programmes not fully taught in English need TOCFL. The MOE publishes a list of fully English-taught programmes (2026 academic year: 58 universities, 522 programme entries; the first 25 per level are copied here) and a list of universities offering tuition and miscellaneous fee discounts to recipients. Programme names in the list are copied as printed in the table cells; some are cut off by the table layout.
institutions_note: Universities and colleges in Taiwan. The applicant applies to admission directly to the university or college, within the deadline each institution sets. The university decides admission; the representative office decides the scholarship. Some universities discount tuition above the NTD 40,000 cap (see the MOE discount list).

summary.detail: Bachelor's degree: scholarship held for a maximum of 4 years. Living allowance NTD 15,000 per month; tuition and miscellaneous fees up to NTD 40,000 per semester. Applicant needs a secondary school graduation diploma and an average grade of at least 3.0 on a 4.5 scale (or the local equivalent). From the 2026 academic year the living allowance of new bachelor's students is paid until 30 June of the graduation year. Minimum semester average to keep the award: 70.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NTD 40,000 per semester
benefits.conditions: The student pays any amount above NTD 40,000 to the university. Some universities discount fees above the cap. Miscellaneous expenses do not include administration fees, thesis supervision fees, insurance, accommodation or internet access.

benefits.limit_text: NTD 15,000 per month (bachelor's); NTD 20,000 per month (master's and doctorate)
benefits.conditions: Paid monthly by the university from the month the recipient actually starts attending. It ends at the maximum period for the level, at five years in total, or on graduation, suspension, withdrawal or revocation. From the 2026 academic year, new bachelor's students are paid until 30 June of their graduation year. Paid only while in Taiwan and enrolled.
Recipients must buy medical and student accident insurance first, then join National Health Insurance when eligible.
The recipient pays it. A student in financial difficulty may ask the university to deduct such costs from the living allowance.

benefits.limit_text: Airfare is not mentioned for the MOE Taiwan Scholarship
benefits.conditions: The MOFA Taiwan Scholarship (a separate scheme) lists economy flights; the MOE Directions do not.

benefits.limit_text: Administration fees, thesis supervision fees and internet access

requirements.text: Taiwan Scholarship application form (each representative office designs its own form). Signed.
Photocopy of the passport or other documentary proof of nationality.
Photocopy of the highest academic award.
Photocopy of academic transcripts. Documents not in Chinese or English need a notarised Chinese or English translation.

Photocopy of proof that you have already applied for admission to a Taiwanese university or college for the coming academic year (for example the application fee receipt, the application form, or the university's acknowledgement notice or email).

Language proficiency certificate: TOCFL result or certificate at Band B level or higher (Terms of Agreement: Level 3 or above) for programmes not fully taught in English; for fully English-taught programmes, the office may accept TOEFL scores, another recognised intermediate English exam, or an English-programme diploma instead.
requirements.conditional_rule: If the local office does not run TOCFL, the Chinese test may be taken at the recipient's own cost by the end of the first semester in Taiwan. Citizens of countries where English is an official language are exempt from the English requirement.

requirements.text: Two letters of recommendation, each written by a school principal, university or college president, professor or tutor. Each writer places the letter in an envelope, seals it and signs personally on the outside.
Any other documents the representative office specifies. The signed Terms of Agreement is among the forms listed on the MOE scholarship page.

Health certificate on the MOE 'Form B' checklist, issued by a hospital and valid for three months. The form lists a chest X-ray for tuberculosis, a stool examination for parasites, a serological test for syphilis, proof of measles and rubella antibodies or vaccination, and an examination for Hansen's disease. The form itself states it is for residence application; the MOE page lists it among the scholarship documents.
requirements.conditional_rule: Stool and Hansen's examination are not required for applicants from designated areas; children and pregnant women are exempt from some tests (as printed on the form).

application_steps.title: Read your representative office's call
application_steps.detail: Each Taiwan representative office (embassy-level office) writes its own guidelines, quota, selection criteria and timetable and publishes them by 31 January each year. In principle the application period runs from 1 February to 31 March, but each office announces its own period (for example, the office in Malaysia took online applications from 1 February to 30 April 2026).

application_steps.title: Apply for admission to a Taiwan university
application_steps.detail: Apply separately and directly to the university or college you want, within its own application period. Each university sets its own deadline. You need proof of this application for the scholarship file.

application_steps.title: Send the scholarship application to the representative office
application_steps.detail: Submit the signed application form, passport copy, highest diploma, transcripts, proof of university application, language certificate and two sealed, signed recommendation letters to the office that handles your country. Submitted documents are not returned. Offices may add their own documents, and some run the application through the MOE online scholarship system.

application_steps.title: The office reviews files and may interview
application_steps.detail: The office reviews documents, and may interview in person or by video, and checks grades, language, character and contribution to Taiwan and your home country. It picks primary candidates and a waiting list. The MOE application-process flowchart marks the interview step as not applying to MOE Taiwan Scholarship applicants, while the MOE process page lists an interview; the Directions say review of documents and/or interviews, so ask your office.

application_steps.title: Results are notified by 31 May
application_steps.detail: In principle, primary candidates and waiting-list candidates are told the result by 31 May. Quotas for each office depend on the MOE budget and the office's performance in the current year.

application_steps.title: Send your university admission letter by 30 June
application_steps.detail: Each primary candidate sends a copy of the admission letter from a Taiwanese university or college to the representative office by 30 June. A candidate who is not admitted loses eligibility, and one who misses the deadline without an accepted reason forfeits it. The place then goes to the next person on the waiting list. Universities send admission decisions by 15 June. The recipient list is final by 31 July.

application_steps.title: Receive the award certificate and arrive in Taiwan on time
application_steps.detail: By 31 July the office issues a scholarship certificate (the duration follows the degree level on the admission letter). Recipients must arrive and register at the university at the set time. A recipient who does not forfeits the scholarship and cannot defer to next year unless the university and the MOE agree beforehand.

application_steps.title: Register, buy insurance and show your residence certificate
application_steps.detail: Each semester present an Alien Resident Certificate showing the purpose 'pursuing studies'. Buy medical and student accident insurance, then join National Health Insurance when allowed. The university holds an orientation and pays the living allowance monthly. Recipients may apply for a work permit (20 hours a week outside summer and winter vacation, permit valid up to six months per semester).

application_steps.title: Meet language, grade and conduct conditions
application_steps.detail: Submit TOCFL at the required level (if not already submitted) by the end of the first semester, or the living allowance is suspended; if missing by the end of the second semester the scholarship is revoked from the third semester. Keep semester averages of at least 70 (bachelor's) or 80 (graduate institutes). Join MOE language and culture activities. Reviews take place by 28 February and 10 September each year.

application_steps.title: Renewal, higher degree and repayment rules
application_steps.detail: The award is renewed each semester if requirements are met. To move to a higher degree, apply by 28 February to the office that gave the first award; this is a new application. A recipient cannot go abroad as an exchange or dual-degree student, or hold another Taiwan government award. Fake documents, concurrent awards and some revocations require repaying the allowances and tuition paid. On finishing, the recipient sends a school report and permanent mailing address to the university and to the representative office in the home country.
